title: 18th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened with committee notices and the first readings of three items: a government bill to amend the Water and Sewerage Act (Law 2020/8), a resolution by Dr. Ahmed Shamheed on electricity and water costs for businesses outside Male', and a Penal Code amendment bill. Members then held the preliminary debate on the Water and Sewerage amendment, which sets a 2027 target for water and sewerage on every inhabited island; speakers from both sides mostly argued over past and present governments' records. Later the resolution on the K-Park housing project in Hulhumale' was debated and, in a vote of 61 in favour with none against, accepted and sent to a committee. The next sitting was set for 23 July 2025.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the amendments and the 2027 deadline, and blamed the long MDP-era governments for unfinished water and sewerage work, citing pipe quality and contractors.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Introduced the government's Water and Sewerage bill, aiming for water and sewerage on all inhabited islands by the end of 2027, and asked members to debate and pass it.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said the bill's sponsor spoke mostly about past governments, and questioned the 2027 target given what he saw as little delivered in two years.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Said water and sewerage works in his area were only 10-15 percent done after years, and hoped the current government completes them as promised.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Backed the bill, saying clean water is a basic right, and pointed to the law's environmental impact report requirement and the roughly 187 inhabited islands to be served by 2027.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Described unfinished projects and contractor problems in his constituency and said services should be given fairly to all islands.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised a point of order saying he had repeatedly submitted questions asking for ministers to appear on the water and sewerage issue.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Thanked the sponsor, said past governments' records must be discussed, and noted projects need funding, design and environmental approval before they can be built.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Said the previous government handed 34 islands to Fenaka with MVR 619 million advance, awaited the Auditor General's report, and called for a national development plan.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Supported the bill and said systems built in islands must be maintained, citing sewerage problems in Fuvahmulah, and backed penalties for misuse.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the amendment and said water and drainage matter for Male' and Hulhumale' too, citing unfinished drainage works on Ameenee Magu.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill, noting that funds may limit the 2027 target, and welcomed its fines for misusing the sewerage system or altering the groundwater layer.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Backed the bill, said Huraa gets water from Fenaka while other Male' Atoll islands get it from STELCO, and asked that Huraa be moved to STELCO and equal subsidies be given.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: On K-Park, said buyers still had not received apartments and a complaint had been filed, and noted the government expects handover within three months.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Called for a special commission on K-Park and for the building to be registered in the names of everyone who paid, and cited 28,000 reported scams from 2021 to 2024.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: As sponsor of the K-Park resolution, asked that it be accepted, called for a solution and for the court hearing to be open to the public.

decisions: Economic Committee membership changed: Ibrahim Nazil replaces Hussain Ziyad from 21 July 2025.
First readings were held for the Water and Sewerage Act amendment bill, a resolution on business electricity and water costs, and a Penal Code amendment bill.
Preliminary debate on the Water and Sewerage Act amendment bill was held but not concluded in this part.
The K-Park resolution was accepted by the Majlis and sent to the committee on domestic governance for study.
Next sitting set for Wednesday 23 July 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accept the resolution on the K-Park residence housing project (62 present, 31 needed)
